a.text: In Ursine mythology, long before the Crystal Age—or perhaps a far earlier age still—
there once lived a giant named Zheuzhyk.
The giant was so tall, the humans could not see him with their eyes. Each slight movement of his sculpted the shapes of the lands.
The Barton Plains are the tracks of his footsteps. The endless Rudokny Mountains were just barely enough to serve as a pillow when he slumbered.
The giant in the legends could not definitively be described as good or evil. He was simply a big, simple existence that the masses below could look up to.
What is difficult to explain, however, is that references to gigantic beings like Zheuzhyk are often found in different mythologies across the land.
These similar stories might perhaps reflect a common characteristic in all human subconscious:
No matter when and where, from the bottom of their hearts, humans seek some kind of a greater power—an enormous being, abstract or specific, that stands in contrast to their minuscule existence.
Mankind is accustomed to worshipping great beings conjured in the imagination, and seeking their projections in reality.
Yet when such a being finally presents itself before the masses in some shape and form—
It never fails to crush their genial fantasies.

steps.name: Unhappy Voice
steps.text: You know, Boris really is a nutjob.

steps.name: Unhappy Voice
steps.text: You saw his arrogant shit face when he met the Marshal too, didn't you? He made a bit of coin these past few years and it gave him a big head.

steps.name: Unhappy Voice
steps.text: Get him a few more coins and he won't even bow to the tsar.

steps.name: Impatient Voice
steps.text: He figures the Marshal doesn't have the balls to try anything funny. Hell, if the Marshal can't scrape together a decent price? He'd probably turn around right there and side with the Third Army instead.

steps.name: Impatient Voice
steps.text: Heh, that's how anyone would play it, with a decent way out.

steps.name: Unhappy Voice
steps.text: A short-sighted businessman sitting on a treasure like this is only ever gonna think about how to use it to fill his pockets. He's never given a single thought to its true worth!

steps.name: Unhappy Voice
steps.text: No wonder he doesn't give the Ursine military the respect we deserve. He can't understand what our land is built on. Really, nobody gives us our due respect!

steps.name: Unhappy Voice
steps.text: If I were the Marshal, I would've slit that coward's throat and stamped my fingerprint on the contract in his blood.

steps.name: Unhappy Voice
steps.text: Heh, if I were the Marshal... I'd order the army to fight to the end, until every Ursine learned to respect us. Not like now... with everyone looking down on us.

steps.name: Impatient Voice
steps.text: Gah... enough of that nonsense!

steps.name: Impatient Voice
steps.text: Do you seriously think the Marshal ever actually backed those morons in the Sixth and Eighth Armies?

steps.name: Impatient Voice
steps.text: With everything they've been up to? They were destined to fail. One does not simply provoke a rebellion in Ursus, especially not with so few guns and battleships... or even with ten times what they had.

steps.name: Impatient Voice
steps.text: They're no different from any of those businessmen. They don't even know where Ursine pride comes from—but the Marshal had it figured out long ago.

steps.name: Impatient Voice
steps.text: So count yourself lucky. You still get to grumble while you're out on a mission, instead of being sent to the Far North to turn to stone with the Infected.

steps.name: Unhappy Voice
steps.text: The hell are you doing?

steps.name: Impatient Voice
steps.text: What I was ordered to do. Making sure everyone's dead.

steps.name: Unhappy Voice
steps.text: We could've at least had him find the others!

steps.name: Impatient Voice
steps.text: Let's not waste more time. We wouldn't even be here today if these white coat bastards had half a mind to cooperate.

steps.name: Impatient Voice
steps.text: There, found one. Hiding under the desk there.

steps.name: Extremely Frightened Voice
steps.text: No! No! Let me go!

steps.name: Extremely Frightened Voice
steps.text: Please! Please don't kill me! I'll tell you whatever you want—

steps.name: Unhappy Voice
steps.text: What do we do? He's willing to cooperate.

steps.name: Impatient Voice
steps.text: Trust me. It'll be faster if we just do this ourselves.

steps.name: Impatient Voice
steps.text: Keep looking. There has to be more of them.

steps.name: Impatient Voice
steps.text: And get a head count. Remember. No one gets out of this place alive.

steps.name: Unhappy Voice
steps.text: I'm starting to get a little annoyed too. This place hardly has any ventilation, and it reeks of blood. Ugh, it's getting my boots all sticky.

steps.name: Unhappy Voice
steps.text: Oh... Found one.

steps.name: Unhappy Voice
steps.text: There's another here.

a.text: An ancient Minoan philosopher once said that 'Man is, by nature, a creative animal.'
By his works, man accumulates experience he then uses to create—in concrete or abstract—and solve the problems he faces.
Such creations fulfill man's needs and assuage his fears. At the same time, they reflect his aesthetics and morals.
Each and every one of mankind's creations is a manifestation of its own traits—
Perhaps it was the same process by which the Creator created mankind.
And among all of mankind's creations, the one that best reflects its innate nature, for good or for evil—
The concept of the 'nation' undoubtedly takes the crown.

steps.name: Timid Researcher
steps.text: Director! They've made it into Area D!

steps.name: Timid Researcher
steps.text: I heard... the sound of fighting... Are they... are they killing people?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Ilia, how much longer?

steps.name: Ilia
steps.text: Forty minutes.

steps.name: Ilia
steps.text: We've done all we can, but it'll take forty more minutes to complete the lockdown procedure.

steps.name: Timid Researcher
steps.text: Do we really have to wait till it's completely locked down?

steps.name: Ilia
steps.text: What else can we do?! Do you want me to hand this thing over to the army completely intact, and let it fall into the butchers' hands, letting them effortlessly massacre even more people?

steps.name: Ilia
steps.text: Blyat! I've lived my whole life as a failure. I refuse to be an accomplice to these murderers even in death!

spans.text: I've lived my whole life as a failure. I refuse to be an accomplice to these murderers even in death!

steps.name: Ilia
steps.text: It's too late...

steps.name: Ilia
steps.text: But how could the butchers work out all our secrets so quickly...?

steps.name: Ilia
steps.text: We have a traitor in our midst... Director, somebody must've sold us out.

steps.name: Ilia
steps.text: Sergei, maybe? I should've known when he kept probing me with all those questions.

steps.name: Ilia
steps.text: Blyat! It must be him... Why? He could have been a good man...

spans.text: It must be him... Why? He could have been a good man...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Calm down, Ilia. Thinking like this will not do us any good right now.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Focus on the task at hand. We still have a chance to salvage something.

steps.name: Ilia
steps.text: Director... It's too late for us... isn't it?

steps.name: Ilia
steps.text: You got my warning. You shouldn't have come back. Even with you here, we still won't finish in—

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Ilia, take the others and go.

steps.name: Ilia
steps.text: Go? Where could we possibly go?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: To Taymyr, in the north. It's close to the Third Army's territory. Andrian wouldn't dare launch a manhunt there.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Hide there and stay far away from the cities. Avoid contact with any factions of the government, and do not believe any promises of protection the Third Army gives you.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Go now. I will stay.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Ilia?

steps.name: Ilia
steps.text: No... I will stay behind.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Ilia.

steps.name: Ilia
steps.text: I won't run. I can't. You shouldn't be entrusting our colleagues' lives to a man like me!

steps.name: Ilia
steps.text: Director Kal'tsit... No, my teacher. The land needs you far more than it needs me. You should go, not me. You should never have come back at all!

steps.name: Ilia
steps.text: Even if you find a way to hide the Originium on your skin, they will find out that you're Infected. Then you will suffer a fate a hundred times worse than a quick and easy death—

spans.text: Even if you find a way to hide the Originium on your skin, they
find out that you're Infected. Then you will suffer a fate a hundred times worse than a quick and easy death—

steps.name: Ilia
steps.text: Besides, only you can lead our innocent colleagues to safety. You can't say no.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But you, too, have a reason to live... Think about Lyudmila, your daughter—

steps.name: Ilia
steps.text: Please, care for her.

steps.name: Ilia
steps.text: Take her away from here, away from this country, and as far away as you can... Heh, I was hoping she would get to study under you for much longer, but it is what it is.

steps.name: Ilia
steps.text: Don't tell her what happened here today. Nothing good will come of it. Let her explore the land in her own way.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I promise you. I will take her far away from Ursus. Until she is able to care for herself, she will be safe.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: And I promise you this. You and your colleagues' work will not go to waste.

steps.name: Ilia
steps.text: That's more than enough for me...

steps.name: Ilia
steps.text: ...It's an intriguing thought. We chose to open this Sarcophagus before, and now we choose to keep it dormant. Which was the right choice?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We did what we thought to be correct. As for the answer, perhaps it is up to Lyudmila... or even her children to determine.

steps.name: Ilia
steps.text: I guess you're right... Now go.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Goodbye, Ilia.

steps.name: Fourth Army Soldier
steps.text: So you're the last one?

steps.name: Ilia
steps.text: The last what?

steps.name: Ilia
steps.text: The last one alive in the lab? Yes. The last one in this country to despise its savagery? Somehow, I doubt it.

steps.name: Fourth Army Soldier
steps.text: You stayed behind. What did you do to the Sarcophagus?

steps.name: Ilia
steps.text: Oh, about ten seconds ago, the Sarcophagus's core function completely locked down. You want to reactivate it? It'll take you lot a century.

steps.name: Ilia
steps.text: You—what are you, vanguards of the murderous Fourth Army? Go back and tell Andrian that his plans to use this beast as a weapon of territorial expansion have just gone belly-up.

steps.name: Ilia
steps.text: Too bad, the glorious Marshal Andrian has failed again and again. His army couldn't conquer a tiny laboratory, or, hell, even a lone, miserable researcher.

steps.name: Ilia
steps.text: Alright, you may exercise your authority to take my life now.

steps.name: Fourth Army Soldier
steps.text: Hm, not bad, for a hard-headed shit...

steps.name: Fourth Army Soldier
steps.text: We'll do it your way.

a.text: For the Empire of Ursus, or perhaps even for all the lands, the Sarcophagus was a groundbreaking discovery, possibly meant for a different era.
I, too, once had ill-timed expectations for it. The tragedy that unfolded before my eyes, in the end, was my punishment.
The innocent sacrifice of the talented researchers in the institute...
No doubt that was a punishment to this country for its hubris.
Even if the effects of this punishment may not be fully realized until much, much later.
In this moment of time, I can offer only a small piece of advice.
If you no longer wish to be dragged into this endless cycle of political conflict and revenge...
If you believe that there yet remains something precious on these lands worth protecting from the mandibles of the manglerbeasts—
Then I ask you to keep this letter and to stop the armies' pursuit of the laboratory's survivors.
This is neither a threat nor a plea.
I simply hope that you will make the right decision based on your interests and conscience.
To Marquess Sheremetyevo Boris
In 1077, a bloody incident occurred in the southeastern corner of Ursus. For an empire that had just suffered a devastating civil war, it was hardly a noticeable incident.

Perhaps it will take a hundred years—when historians revisit these turbulent times in their piles of old writings—for everyone to truly understand that what happened at the research institute in Chernobog was both emblematic of its era and a seed.
Even if, at this moment in time, it is buried deep under the Ursine permafrost, waiting for its time to sprout.

steps.name: Young Voice
steps.text: Where am I?

steps.name: Young Voice
steps.text: What happened to the court martial? What happened to due process?

steps.name: Young Voice
steps.text: Why did you bring me here? And where are my men?

steps.name: Grumpy Voice
steps.text: Shut up.

steps.name: Young Voice
steps.text: You would have to kill me.

steps.name: Grumpy Voice
steps.text: You're on death row. It doesn't make a difference whether we kill you now or later.

steps.name: Grumpy Voice
steps.text: Too bad for you, the bigwigs don't have time to deal with seditious leadership like yourself, so...

steps.name: Grumpy Voice
steps.text: You'll just have to hold up here. Listen to how your men in the other rooms stay quiet?

steps.name: Young Voice
steps.text: I'm a soldier, not a criminal. The same goes for my men!

steps.name: Grumpy Voice
steps.text: From the moment you worked up the arrogance to rise against the Marshal, your entire formation ceased to be a part of the glorious Fourth Army.

steps.name: Young Voice
steps.text: I did the right thing, and all the warriors you have dismissed as traitors, and in fact all Ursines of conscience, know that this is the right thing to do.

steps.name: Grumpy Voice
steps.text: No, Captain Yakov Petrov.

steps.name: Grumpy Voice
steps.text: What you did was the foolish thing to do, and you dragged your family and your friends into this mess.

steps.name: Quiet Boy
steps.text: Mother, please, sit down first... You're shaking.

steps.name: Quiet Boy
steps.text: The people from the army have already gone.

steps.name: Dazed Woman
steps.text: Army... Yakov...

steps.name: Dazed Woman
steps.text: Is that you, Yakov?

steps.name: Dazed Woman
steps.text: You are back?

steps.name: Dazed Woman
steps.text: But the apple trees have yet to blossom... It's too soon for your summer vacation.

steps.name: Dazed Woman
steps.text: Has Marshal Andrian been treating you well? Has he been bringing you on his adventures? What about the clothes I had them bring to you? Did they fit?

steps.name: Dazed Woman
steps.text: I can't see well, so I couldn't sew your name onto them... but Sofia helped. You've always loved her handicrafts—

steps.name: Dazed Woman
steps.text: Sofia?

steps.name: Quiet Boy
steps.text: Mother.

steps.name: Dazed Woman
steps.text: You're not Sofia.

steps.name: Quiet Boy
steps.text: Nor am I Yakov. I am neither Brother nor Sister.

steps.name: Dazed Woman
steps.text: Who are you? Why are you in my home? Somebody—

steps.name: Quiet Boy
steps.text: Mother, I'm Tulin, your young son who has been away for a long time. You remember me, do you not?

steps.name: Quiet Boy
steps.text: The servants have been dismissed, and the butler has left.

steps.name: Dazed Woman
steps.text: What are you saying?

steps.name: Quiet Boy
steps.text: Yakov is in prison. Sofia is married, but she is busy scrambling about in Deity Grypherburg, desperately trying to get him out. She needs money to resolve some issues, and we must help.

steps.name: Quiet Boy
steps.text: Moreover, we cannot embroil the innocent in a fate they do not deserve, can we?

steps.name: Quiet Boy
steps.text: *sigh...*

steps.name: Quiet Boy
steps.text: No matter the case, please listen to what I have to say, Mother. You may never have heard these things, but this letter was written by Yakov in prison.

steps.name: Quiet Boy
steps.text: Let me read it for you...
The boy says and opens the envelope, only to find a blank sheet of paper.
In an instant, his face turns as white as the sheet in his hands.

steps.name: Dazed Woman
steps.text: Yakov... Isn't Yakov in the army?

steps.name: Quiet Boy
steps.text: The army has been here, Mother.
The boy folds the sheet of paper in half, bit by bit, as if needing the time to slow down and process the truth.
Then, he puts the small and neatly folded square into his breast pocket, normally occupied by a handkerchief, to keep it close to his heart.

steps.name: Quiet Boy
steps.text: They said that because of the role that Yakov played in the Fourth Army's mutiny...

steps.name: Quiet Boy
steps.text: The Petrovs have been stripped of nobility and are now mere commoners... to be exiled to the Northern Tundra Mines, Mining Zone No. 9.

steps.name: Quiet Boy
steps.text: We set out tomorrow.

steps.name: Despairing Infected
steps.text: Old Peter's buried. It's time for us to go.

steps.name: Despairing Infected
steps.text: First, it was our children, then our wives, and then our parents... How many more bodies will we have to bury?

steps.name: Despairing Infected
steps.text: What are you doing, writing a letter? Is it to your mother?

steps.name: Quiet Boy
steps.text: No... Not a letter. I'm just trying to put everything I see into words. If the chance ever comes, I hope people will come to know all that has happened.

steps.name: Despairing Infected
steps.text: You still have the strength for that? I must say, I really envy you.

steps.name: Despairing Infected
steps.text: I can't walk very far, and we still have yet to make it to the Northern Tundra.

steps.name: Quiet Boy
steps.text: It's only been three months since we left Omska.

steps.name: Quiet Boy
steps.text: It'll probably be spring again by the time we make it to the mines.

steps.name: Despairing Infected
steps.text: Spring... Haha! Spring!

steps.name: Despairing Infected
steps.text: My sweet summer child. You think there is spring in the tundra...?

steps.name: Quiet Boy
steps.text: Right, spring. As long as we make it there.

steps.name: Despairing Infected
steps.text: Your mother was spared because she's blind and off her rocker.

steps.name: Despairing Infected
steps.text: She doesn't have to suffer the pain of exile, and you are spared from having to bury her like a nameless woman. Thanks to that, you are so optimistic, you might as well be a lunatic.

steps.name: Despairing Infected
steps.text: But... what gives you the right?

steps.name: Despairing Infected
steps.text: What gives you the right?

steps.name: Despairing Infected
steps.text: You, too, are an exiled criminal, and yet someone like you gets special treatment. You don't have to watch as every member of your family slowly takes their last breaths, as their bodies slowly turn cold.

steps.name: Despairing Infected
steps.text: Is it because I was only a dime-a-dozen porter before I turned into an Infected?

steps.name: Despairing Infected
steps.text: What did I do wrong? And what did you do right?

spans.text: What did I do wrong? And what did

steps.text: The Infected murmurs. He wants to scream the thoughts in his mind out loud more than anybody, but he is trapped under the watchful gaze of the guards.
The boy shakes his head and moves up closer toward the Infected.

steps.name: Quiet Boy
steps.text: I was privileged, yes... And it wasn't because of my own hard work. For that, I feel ashamed.

steps.name: Quiet Boy
steps.text: But the question you posed is one that I am seeking the answer to myself.

steps.name: Despairing Infected
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Quiet Boy
steps.text: Why are some of us born privileged, while others are born disdained? Why do we stand in opposition to each other, even though we are all humans? What can we do to break free of the status quo?

steps.name: Quiet Boy
steps.text: I will tell you. I don't know.

steps.name: Quiet Boy
steps.text: But my instinct tells me that we need to at least survive and stand back up.

steps.name: Quiet Boy
steps.text: It's only when we stand together and combine our strength that we are able to keep thinking about where the problem lies and figure out a way to change something.

steps.name: Despairing Infected
steps.text: What are you talking about—
The boy suddenly lifts his head and looks into the Infected man's perplexed eyes.

steps.name: Quiet Boy
steps.text: Just pretend I'm talking nonsense.

steps.name: Quiet Boy
steps.text: The way I see it, people like you with nothing to their name are the true masters of the land.

steps.name: Quiet Boy
steps.text: For the time being, please, climb onto my back. At the very least, I still have some strength in me. I can carry you for a while.

a.text: '...In Iberia, people almost never turn their gazes upon one another, as if making eye contact were sinful, and as if doing so would violate a deeply held creed.
'I have also witnessed similar behaviors in the mines of Ursus, the slums of Leithanien, and the underground factories of Victoria.

'At first, I surmised that they feared seeing in their soot-covered faces the same despair they felt in their hearts. It was only later that I realized it was because, their eyes had little room for anything beyond the urgency of survival.

'That being the case, who could blame them for their silence and for failing to notice their fellow man, for failing to look to a future even further away, for failing to stand together to rise against their oppressors?'

'The land sprawls far and wide. I traveled throughout Ursus, and then made my way to even farther lands. On my way, I continued to tell those who had lost everything—or perhaps have never truly had anything: You are the true masters of the land.

'As things currently stand, and we have yet to see any real change, my words feel like little more than mockery, yet I need to keep telling them. It is only by planting these seeds that they may subconsciously realize the truth behind my words and let them sprout within their hearts.
'When one truly has nothing, one has nothing to lose, granting the most resolute of resolves. The same truth lies within us all.'

steps.name: Nimble Miner
steps.text: Boss!

steps.name: Nimble Miner
steps.text: We're all packed up, ready to go. How about you?

steps.name: The Pensive Youth
steps.text: Hm...

steps.name: Nimble Miner
steps.text: Boss?

steps.name: The Pensive Youth
steps.text: Uh... Oh! Right. Let's get going.

steps.name: The Pensive Youth
steps.text: Thanks for coming to get me. I'm all packed up too—

steps.name: The Pensive Youth
steps.text: Uhh.

steps.name: Nimble Miner
steps.text: You dug out all this stuff again? What a mess... Here, I'll help you pack up.

steps.name: The Pensive Youth
steps.text: Thanks!

steps.name: Nimble Miner
steps.text: I came to the mines late, I've never seen the one who sent you the letters. Did they really leave the mines and keep on writing to you?

steps.name: The Pensive Youth
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Nimble Miner
steps.text: First time I've ever heard of anyone missing life in the mines so much.

steps.name: The Pensive Youth
steps.text: Perhaps it's not the mines that he misses, but the people.

steps.name: The Pensive Youth
steps.text: As I remember, when the news of political prisoners getting pardoned first got here to the Northern Tundra, his first reaction wasn't one of joy. It was worry.

steps.name: The Pensive Youth
steps.text: He was worried that we wouldn't be able to leave like him, and that his theories would never be proven...

steps.name: Nimble Miner
steps.text: But he still left in the end.

steps.name: The Pensive Youth
steps.text: Of course. He said he'd travel all across Ursus, and now we're leaving this place behind too, aren't we?

steps.name: Nimble Miner
steps.text: Then let's get going, Boss.

steps.name: Nimble Miner
steps.text: Right, I started calling you 'Boss' because that's what everyone here calls you, but I've been thinking, you've got to have an actual name, right?

steps.name: The Pensive Youth
steps.text: Huh, have I really never told you?

steps.name: The Pensive Youth
steps.text: Hm... Tulin. You can call me Tulin.

steps.name: Nimble Miner
steps.text: Hell yeah, 'Tulin.' Good name. Here, I'll help you up.

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: Thank you...

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: Yeah, let's hurry and get out of here.

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: While the snow is still calm, and before the ones in the warm houses change their minds.

a.text: '...Investigation shows that the extremely provocative messages left behind by the instigators are all quotations from Yakov Petrov, a war criminal who got what he deserved during the Great Rebellion.
'While on death row, he wrote a will...'
'Whose fault was the Katorga Uprising? What should we do now? How do we save these young people who know nothing but rebellion?'
'While the Chairman's condition is now stable, the fiend behind the assassination attempt remains at large.
'The Deity Grypherburg Police call on everyone to stay indoors after nightfall to avoid arousing suspicion and interfering with the search operation.'

steps.name: Solemn Soldier
steps.text: (Flips through the newspaper)

steps.name: Solemn Soldier
steps.text: (Closes the newspaper)

steps.name: Solemn Soldier
steps.text: Zdravstvuyte, gospodin. Could you fetch me a fresher newspaper?

spans.text: Could you fetch me a fresher newspaper?

steps.name: Nervous Servant
steps.text: Uh. I-I'm afraid that will require prior approval.

steps.name: Nervous Servant
steps.text: This lounge's newspapers and reading material are maintained daily by a page. I can't just conjure up one out of thin air for you.

steps.name: Nervous Servant
steps.text: Besides, you are an Infected. You may have been let in, but I don't know if you really have authorization to read this—

steps.name: Hasty Noble
steps.text: *cough*!

steps.name: Nervous Servant
steps.text: Gospodin Gorchikov—I mean, General!

steps.name: Hasty Noble
steps.text: You may call me Vice Chairman here. Thank you for your help. I will handle the rest.

steps.name: Nervous Servant
steps.text: What? Could that be... is this your guest?

steps.name: Nervous Servant
steps.text: Bozhe moy... I'm so stupid! Please accept my sincerest apologies, gospodin, for my words—

spans.text: ... I'm so stupid! Please accept my sincerest apologies, gospodin, for my words—

steps.name: Solemn Soldier
steps.text: So it goes. What you said is the truth.

steps.name: Solemn Soldier
steps.text: Indeed, I am an Infected.

steps.name: Nervous Servant
steps.text: The newspaper. You, I... I—

steps.name: Hasty Noble
steps.text: *sigh...* Just do as I said, and let me handle the rest!

steps.name: Solemn Soldier
steps.text: 'General?'

steps.name: Hasty Noble
steps.text: Please, don't tease me... You know better than anyone whether or not I will become general.

steps.name: Solemn Soldier
steps.text: You weren't so hard on yourself before, Vasily.

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: And you weren't this easy to talk to, for an officer of the army.

steps.name: Solemn Soldier
steps.text: The man who stands before you now is a mere Infected warrior, no longer an Imperial Guard instructor.

steps.name: Solemn Soldier
steps.text: You still remember my name, do you not? Call me Hellagur.

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: Very good, Gospodin Hellagur. How does it feel to return to Grypherburg? This is hardly a time for sightseeing, but still.

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: It's a lot quieter than I expected. A lot of things have changed, so much so that hardly anything from times gone by still remains.

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: Right. So much has changed, and who could say whether these changes are for the better or worse?

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: The businessmen have gotten richer. Thanks to that, the city has become a more beautiful place. At the same time, modesty and all our other virtues are now valued less.

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: Perhaps you've heard already. His Imperial Majesty is going to build a so-called 'citizens' forum' and hand over all decision-making to the common folk of Grypherburg.

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: And now, we can all say that the nobles have finally given up on the one job they still had and handed it over to the commoners.

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: It sounds like you don't agree with this at all.

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: It's not up to me to agree or disagree, but if there's someone out there who can solve all these problems facing society, it doesn't matter who that person is.

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: This doesn't sound like something the vice chairman, with all his authority, would say.

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: I've never been one eager to put my power on full display. You know that better than anyone.

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: Come to think of it, I'm surprised they didn't confiscate your blade when you entered the city.

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: Oh, this. All they did was make a note of it. I didn't receive too much... special treatment. This is only a replica, and one that hasn't been sharpened. It's as lethal as a piece of scrap metal. Perhaps that's why.

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: Where's the real one?

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: I gave it to someone I trust.

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: Someone you trust...

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: I understand you have a daughter.

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: Yes, I do. If we find the time later, I would love to introduce you to her. She has heard many stories of your achievements, and she respects you deeply.

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: And it's not just her. Many in today's Imperial Guard still remember your name.

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: It's been some years since we hung up our hats, but those stories yet fly over the Imperial Guard Academy like a banner. At your convenience, I'd like to take you for a visit.

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: You have my thanks for keeping those sacrifices so close to your heart, but I truly have no intention of serving as a banner ever again.

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: I am here for another reason. Surely you must already know that Rhodes Island has established an office here in Grypherburg.

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: I am well aware. I even signed a few documents in the Chairman's stead.

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: *sigh...* Even if our stance on the Infected has relaxed, the conflicts regarding them remain as sharp as ever.

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: Still, if we're speaking of you personally—I would be happy to take this chance to restore your honors in Grypherburg.

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: I don't need the empire to restore my identity or honor.

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: Then what do you need?

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: Simply put, what Rhodes Island needs is precisely what I need.

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: More specifically, you mean—

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: 'Please inform Chairman Witte that the designated Rhodes Islanders have departed for Deity Grypherburg.'

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: If my timing is right, they should have already made it to the office.

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: Oh...

steps.name: Nervous Soldier
steps.text: Chairman—

steps.name: Nervous Soldier
steps.text: Is the Chairman here?!

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: I am the vice chairman. What's the matter?

steps.name: Nervous Soldier
steps.text: I... I have a report!

steps.name: Nervous Soldier
steps.text: Th-The First Army—
The soldier tries his best to get a noun out of his mouth, but he finds himself frozen when he spots Hellagur standing to the side.
Vasily shakes his head to signal that there is nothing to worry about.

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: What of the First Army?

steps.name: Nervous Soldier
steps.text: The new weapon of mass destruction that the First Army has been developing... The firing test was successful!

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: And, what's the problem?

steps.name: Nervous Soldier
steps.text: The problem is... the weapon doesn't use Originium... or any energy source that we've ever employed!

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: What?
